unit.title: Develop and update hospitality industry/job knowledge

summary: This unit gives you the industry and job knowledge that every villa or hotel worker needs: the sectors of Jamaican tourism, the kinds of accommodation and meal plans, the main resort areas and attractions, the visitors and the seasons, the organisations that run and support tourism, the types of tourism and current trends, the jobs and careers in a villa, and how to keep your own knowledge up to date. With this knowledge you can give guests correct advice and plan your own career.

blocks.p: Guests ask villa staff a hundred questions: where to eat, how to reach Dunn's River Falls, whether it is safe to swim, what 'all-inclusive' means. A worker who knows the answers gives better service and is trusted. A worker who guesses spoils the guest's holiday. This unit is for HOSPITALITY VILLA/PROPERTIES SERVICES LEVEL 2 trainees. It gives you the general knowledge that sits behind every other unit.

head: What you must be able to do
What this means at the villa
rows: Describe the tourism and hospitality industry
Name the sectors and give an example of each
Explain how the sectors depend on each other
Know kinds of accommodation and meal plans
Hotels, resorts, villas, guest houses, bed and breakfasts, eco-lodges
EP, CP, MAP, AP and all-inclusive
Know Jamaica's resort areas and attractions
Where they are, which parish, what they offer, how to reach them
Understand visitors, seasons and the economy
Stopover and cruise visitors, where they come from
Peak, low and hurricane seasons; foreign exchange, jobs, linkages
Ministry of Tourism, JTB, TPDCo, JHTA, HEART/NSTA Trust
Know the types of tourism and the trends
Eco, heritage, community, wedding, sports, health, MICE
Online booking and reviews; protecting beaches and reefs
Know the jobs and your own career path
Villa jobs and how they fit together
Job description, training and the next step up
Keep your knowledge up to date
Use reliable sources; check before you tell a guest

blocks.note: How you are assessed: theory papers (multiple-choice questions, short answers and essays) and group practical tasks: a visitor guide to a resort area and a display of job cards, a career map and a news board. Facts in the practical must be correct, current and backed by sources with dates.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.note: Facts such as opening times, entry fees, flight schedules and local rules change. This kit teaches the stable facts. For anything that can change, **check a current source**, and say so to the guest.
blocks.label: Tip

blocks.p: **Tourism** is people travelling away from home for pleasure, rest or business and staying for a short time. A person who does this is a **tourist** or **visitor**. **Hospitality** is the part of the industry that welcomes, feeds and houses them. Together they are one of Jamaica's largest earners of foreign exchange and one of its biggest employers.

head: Sector
What it does
Examples in Jamaica
rows: All-inclusive resorts, hotels, villas, guest houses, apartments, eco-lodges
Restaurants, jerk centres, bars, cafés, hotel and villa kitchens
Airlines, cruise lines, licensed tour buses, taxis, car rental firms
Dunn's River Falls, river rafting, great houses, museums, music events and festivals
Put together and sell trips and holiday packages
Companies that sell a flight, hotel and tours as one package
Craft markets, spas, tour guides, souvenir shops

blocks.note: A **tour operator** puts together and sells trips or holiday packages. It does not clean hotel rooms, fly the planes or cook the guests' meals.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.p: All the sectors are linked. If the taxi is late, the hotel is blamed. If the meal is poor, the whole holiday suffers. This is why every worker's service matters.

ul: **Foreign exchange** means money from other countries, such as US dollars, that visitors bring into Jamaica. It pays for imports such as fuel and medicine.
Tourism creates jobs directly (hotel staff, guides, drivers) and indirectly (farmers, builders, craft sellers, laundries).
The legal currency of Jamaica is the **Jamaican dollar (J$)**. Many businesses also accept US$, at a rate that the manager sets.

blocks.p: A **linkage** is when tourism businesses buy from local producers. A villa that buys fruit and vegetables from farmers in St Elizabeth, fish from fishermen, or crafts from a local market is creating linkages between tourism and farming, fishing and craft. Linkages keep more money in the local economy and give guests fresh local food.

head: Benefits
Problems if not managed
rows: Damage to beaches, reefs and forests
Pressure on water, power and waste services
Markets for farmers, fishers and craft workers
Prices rise for local people in busy areas
Roads, airports and other facilities improved
Money leaks overseas if goods are imported

sections.title: Kinds of accommodation and meal plans

head: Kind
What it is
Typical features
rows: A usually large property with one price that covers the room, meals, drinks and many activities
Many rooms, pools, restaurants and bars, entertainment team
Rooms and services rented by the night; meals and extras often paid for separately
Front desk, restaurant, housekeeping, sometimes a pool and a gym
A private house for one group of guests, often with its own staff
Kitchen, pool, garden; cook, housekeeper, gardener, sometimes a butler and a driver
Few rooms, home-style meals, personal service
A small, often family-run place that offers a room and a morning meal
A small, natural-style place in the countryside built to have little harm on the environment
Solar power, local materials, nature activities
Own kitchen; cleaning and services may be extra

blocks.p: Rate sheets use short codes. Learn them.

head: Plan
Letters
What is included
rows: Continental Plan or Bed and Breakfast
The room and a breakfast (some places use CP for a light continental breakfast)
The room and all three meals each day
The room, meals, drinks (including alcohol) and many activities in one price

blocks.note: Codes can differ a little between properties. Always read the rate sheet or ask the manager before you answer a guest.
blocks.label: Tip

ul: A **rate** is the price per night. It changes with the season, the room type and the meal plan.
**Peak (high) season rates** are higher; **low (off) season rates** are often lower.
A rate may be quoted in J$ or US$ and may not include GCT or service charge. Check what is shown.

blocks.p: Know where the main places are, the parish they are in, what they offer and how visitors reach them. A guest will expect you to know.

head: Place
Parish
Known for
rows: Sangster International Airport, resorts, beaches, nightlife, Reggae Sumfest (festival)
Seven Mile Beach, sunsets, cliffs, relaxed resorts and villas
Dunn's River Falls, cruise port, north-coast resorts, waterfalls and gardens
Georgian historic town, cruise ship port, nearby river tours
Rafting on the Rio Grande, the Blue Lagoon, lush green hills and beaches
Capital city; music, culture, history, museums, business; Norman Manley International Airport
Historic town on the harbour, once a pirate port
Quiet south-coast community tourism, fishing, small guest houses and villas
Boat safaris to see crocodiles on the Black River
Jamaica's best-known coffee, hiking trails, cool air

blocks.note: Negril is the resort town of Seven Mile Beach. Ocho Rios is in St Ann. Montego Bay is in St James. Port Antonio is in Portland. Treasure Beach is on the south coast. Kingston is the capital city.
blocks.label: Remember

head: Airport
City
Most useful for
rows: Montego Bay, Negril, Falmouth and the north-west
Kingston, the Blue Mountains and the south and east

ul: Smaller airstrips serve some areas; ask for the current information.
Many visitors travel by licensed taxi, shuttle or tour bus. Check the villa's own transfer arrangements.
The north-coast road links Montego Bay, Falmouth, Ocho Rios and Port Antonio, and travel times change with roadworks and traffic. **Do not quote exact driving times unless you have checked them.**
Say what you know and say when you are unsure. 'I will find out and come back to you' is better than a wrong answer.
Recommend licensed operators, restaurants and guides.
Mention safety tips: swim where lifeguards are or where the villa advises, keep valuables locked, use licensed transport, wear sunscreen.
Know the emergency numbers: **119 police; 110 fire and ambulance**. Display them.

blocks.note: A guest asks where to find a vegetarian meal in Negril, or a quiet beach on the south coast. Your answer comes from what you know of the area and the guest's tastes and budget. It does not come only from your cousin's restaurant.
blocks.label: Jamaica

sections.title: Visitors, seasons and the hurricane season

head: Visitor
Description
rows: Stays at least one night in the country
Arrives by ship and usually spends the day or part of a day ashore while the ship is in port
Jamaicans overseas and others who stay with family
Comes for work, a conference or a meeting

ul: Most stopover visitors come from **North America** (the USA and Canada), then Europe and other Caribbean countries.
Cruise passengers spend little time and money in each port, so their needs are short tours, craft shopping and a meal. They are not staying in a hotel near the port for two weeks.

head: Season
When
What it means for the villa
rows: Busiest; highest rates; full bookings; longer hours; bring in extra staff
The quieter months of the year
Fewer visitors; lower rates; time for deep cleaning, repairs, painting and staff training
June to November (the Atlantic hurricane season)
Possible storms; the villa must have a hurricane plan; may affect arrival, supplies and safety

blocks.p: The hurricane season overlaps with the low season. It does not run from December to March, and it is not a single month.

flow: Listen to official warnings (the Meteorological Service and ODPEM)
Bring in loose items, shutter windows, secure the pool area
Check food, water, fuel, torches and first aid
Contact guests and arrange safe movement
After the storm, check for damage and report it

blocks.note: Villa staff follow the manager's instructions and the official advice. Do not repeat rumours about a storm to guests. Give them the official information.
blocks.label: Safety

head: Type
What it is
Example
rows: Visiting natural areas such as forests, rivers and wildlife while helping to protect them
Blue Mountains hikes, river tours, Black River safari
Visiting historic places and learning about culture
Visiting local communities, which share the benefits
Treasure Beach experiences led by local people
Couples who come to marry or honeymoon
Wedding at a villa or beach
A company conference at a hotel
Visitors who come for a sport or festival
Visitors who come for treatment, rest or wellness
A day at Falmouth or Ocho Rios

ul: **Online booking and reviews**: most guests book online and read reviews first. Every stay matters because guests share their views.
**Sustainability**: visitors come for nature, and reefs protect the coast from waves. Villas save water and energy, reduce plastic and protect beaches and reefs.
**Authentic local experiences**: guests want local food, music and stories, not only the beach.
**Wellness and slow travel**: yoga, spa and quiet places.
**Safety and health**: guests expect high standards of hygiene and clear information.

blocks.p: Staff can respond by giving friendly service, answering online reviews politely when asked to, using local products, saving water and electricity, and telling guests how to care for the beach and reef.

head: Organisation
Role
rows: The government ministry in charge of tourism policy
Markets and promotes Jamaica as a place to visit
Improves the tourism product: sets and inspects standards, supports licensing, runs training such as Team Jamaica
An association of hotels and tourism businesses; represents and supports its members
Trains people for jobs, including tourism, and awards NVQ-J certificates (through accredited training centres)
A fund supported by tourism that pays for improving the product (check current details)

blocks.note: Do not mix these up. The JTB markets Jamaica; TPDCo improves and checks the product and trains workers; the JHTA is an association of businesses; the Ministry makes policy.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.p: Hotels, villas, guest houses, attractions and tour operators must be licensed. The licence shows that the property meets standards for safety and service. A licence does **not** give the right to set any price, to ignore health rules or to leave staff untrained.
Team Jamaica is TPDCo's training programme for front-line tourism workers: good service to visitors and knowledge of Jamaica. Ask your supervisor whether you can attend.

sections.title: Jobs and careers in a villa

blocks.h: Main jobs in a staffed villa

head: Job
Main duties
rows: Runs the property, guests, staff, bookings and budget
Plans and prepares meals; follows food safety rules
Looks after guests' personal needs: unpacking, drinks, arrangements, tours
Cleans and prepares rooms, laundry, linen
Garden, grounds and often pool care
Keeps the pool safe and clean, towels, safety

blocks.p: The team depends on each other. The housekeeper tells the cook about guest allergies noticed in the room; the driver tells the manager when guests arrive; the manager tells the gardener when guests want to use the pool.
Your **job description** says what your job is, your duties and the standards you must meet. Read it. It is where you find the duties and standards of your own job, not on a booking form or a menu.

flow: Know your job description and do it well
Ask your supervisor what skills the next job needs
Take training (NVQ-J units, Team Jamaica, first aid, food handler's course)
Take on extra tasks and show you are reliable
Apply when a higher job opens

ul: A housekeeper who wants to become a supervisor should **do more training and ask her manager what skills are needed**. She should not wait to be noticed, stop doing her own work or announce to guests that she is already the supervisor.
Keep a record of your training and certificates.
Qualifications you can get through HEART/NSTA Trust and the NCTVET system include NVQ-J certificates at Levels 1 to 5.

head: Possible career steps
Skills to build
rows: Room attendant → housekeeping supervisor → head housekeeper
Quality checks, leading a team, stock control

sections.title: Keeping your knowledge up to date

blocks.p: Guests rely on you for correct advice. Attractions open and close, prices and times change, and new rules appear. Keeping up to date gives guests correct advice and good service. It does not mean you can skip training.

head: Source
Why it is useful
rows: Ministry of Tourism and Meteorological Service
Current events and road or weather information
The villa's manager and guest information sheet
Rules of the property and local contacts
What guests value and what to improve
Colleagues and local operators who know the area

ul: Anything on social media that has no named, official source
A first-time visitor's opinion
What you were taught at school years ago, without checking
A friend's 'I heard that...'

flow: Check a reliable source (manager, official site, operator)
Check the date of the information
Write it in the log book or guest information sheet for the next person

blocks.note: Never say a new attraction does not exist just to avoid looking unsure, and never make up details to satisfy the guest.
blocks.label: Safety

blocks.p: Feedback shows what guests value and what to improve. Thank the guest, write it down and tell your supervisor. A good worker changes what they do because of it. It is not used to decide which guests to avoid.
In a visitor guide or a news board, write each source and its date. This lets the next reader check that the information is current.
Tick each statement when you can do it without looking at your notes.

ul: I can name the sectors of the industry and give an example of each.
I can explain foreign exchange, linkages and the benefits and problems of tourism.
I can explain the kinds of accommodation and the meal plans EP, CP, MAP, AP and all-inclusive.
I can place the main resort areas in their parishes and say what they are known for.
I can say which airport serves which area.
I can describe stopover visitors and cruise passengers and where most visitors come from.
I can state the peak season and the hurricane season and what each means for a villa.
I can describe the types of tourism, including MICE, eco, heritage and community tourism.
I can state what the JTB, TPDCo, JHTA, HEART/NSTA Trust and the Ministry of Tourism do.
I can describe the main villa jobs and plan a career step.
I can use reliable sources, check dates and say 'I will find out'.
I can use guest feedback to improve.

Visitor who stays at least one night

Room only / room and breakfast / room, breakfast and dinner / room and three meals
One price for the room, meals, drinks and many activities

c1.title: A family plans a week from a villa in Negril
c1.text: The Ramsay family from Toronto are staying for a week at a villa in Negril. Over breakfast they ask Mrs. Daley, the villa manager, for advice. They would like one day trip to see waterfalls and a cruise-port town, one day to see crocodiles, and a quiet day on a south-coast beach. They also ask what the hurricane season means for their trip, which is in October.

c2.title: A confusing rate sheet
c2.text: A travel agent in Atlanta sends a rate sheet to the same villa. It lists the 'MAP' rate and the 'EP' rate for next March. The villa's new trainee, Jodian, is asked to explain the plans by email to a guest who wants a cheaper rate and a lot of flexibility to eat out. Another guest asks why the rate for March is higher than the rate for June.

c3.title: Pool season at a villa in Treasure Beach
c3.text: In June, bookings at a villa in Treasure Beach are slow. Owner Mr. Wright decides to use the quiet weeks to repaint, service the pool pump and train staff. He also buys vegetables from a farmer in nearby Junction instead of from a supplier in Kingston. Some staff say tourism does not help local people because guests only stay inside the villa.

c4.title: A gardener who wants to move up
c4.text: Andre has been the gardener at a villa in Port Antonio for two years and likes talking to guests. He tells his manager he wants to become a butler and one day a villa manager. He is not sure what to do. A guest asks him whether a new attraction near Boston Bay is open, and he has never heard of it.

c5.title: Questions from a visitor to Kingston
c5.text: A visitor staying at a villa in Kingston asks Shaniqua, the housekeeper, three questions: which airport she will use to fly home to Miami, which parish Port Royal is in, and what a 'MICE' group is, as she saw the word on a hotel board. Shaniqua is not sure about the last answer.

questions.q: Which area should Mrs. Daley suggest for a waterfall visit and a cruise-port town in the same day?
o: Treasure Beach in St Elizabeth
Ocho Rios in St Ann, near Dunn's River Falls
Black River in St Elizabeth
Port Royal in Kingston and St Andrew
questions.why: Ocho Rios in St Ann is known for Dunn's River Falls and a cruise port. Treasure Beach and Black River are on the south coast, and Port Royal is a historic harbour town near Kingston.

questions.q: Where can the family see crocodiles on a boat safari?
o: Seven Mile Beach in Negril
The Rio Grande in Portland
Falmouth in Trelawny
Black River in St Elizabeth
questions.why: Boat safaris for crocodiles take place on the Black River in St Elizabeth. The Rio Grande is known for rafting.

questions.q: Mrs. Daley recommends a safe way to reach the waterfalls. Which is best?
o: Book a licensed tour operator or a licensed taxi
Accept a lift from a friendly stranger on the beach
Hire any unmarked car that stops outside the villa
Walk the whole way, whatever the weather and time
questions.why: Licensed operators and taxis are checked and accountable, which is why villas recommend them. Unmarked cars and strangers are a safety risk for visitors.

questions.q: What should Mrs. Daley say about October?
o: It is the peak season, with the highest rates of the year
It is a safe month because storms only come in December
It is in the hurricane season, so follow official warnings
It is the month with no hurricane risk, as it is so hot
questions.why: The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June to November, so October is in it. The peak tourist season is mid-December to mid-April.

questions.q: What does the MAP rate include?
o: The room only
The room and all three meals each day
The room, breakfast and dinner
The room, all meals and all drinks
questions.why: MAP is the Modified American Plan: room, breakfast and dinner. EP is room only, AP is three meals, and all-inclusive includes drinks and activities.

questions.q: Which plan suits a guest who wants to eat out as much as possible?
o: EP, the room only
AP, three meals a day
MAP, breakfast and dinner
All-inclusive, with every drink
questions.why: With the room only, the guest pays only for meals actually eaten at the villa and is free to eat out. The other plans include meals the guest may not use.

questions.q: Why is the villa's rate for March higher than the rate for June?
o: March has more days than June
The villa raises rates in months with fewer storms only for new guests
June has the hurricane season, so rates are set by the government
March is in the peak season and June is in the low season
questions.why: Rates rise in the busy peak season (about mid-December to mid-April) and are often lower in the low season. Rates are set by the property, not by the government.

questions.q: What is the best use of the slow weeks in June?
o: Closing all training until the next peak season
Deep cleaning, repairs, painting and staff training
Cutting every worker's hours to zero
Asking guests to repair and paint the rooms
questions.why: Low season gives time for maintenance and training that cannot be done when the villa is full. Cutting hours or training wastes the chance.

questions.q: Mr. Wright buys vegetables from a farmer in Junction. What is this an example of?
o: A loss of foreign exchange
A linkage between tourism and farming
A conflict of interest
An import from another country
questions.why: A linkage is when tourism businesses buy from local producers, keeping money in the community. Importing would take money out of Jamaica.

questions.q: How can the staff's claim that tourism does not help local people be answered?
o: Agree, and encourage guests to stay inside the villa
Say that most of the money goes overseas in any case
Point to the jobs and the local suppliers it supports
Say that only foreign owners really gain from it
questions.why: Tourism creates jobs and markets for local farmers, fishers and craft workers. Staying inside the villa does not mean the villa buys nothing locally.

questions.q: What is Andre's best first step?
o: Ask his manager what skills a butler needs and take training
Start giving orders to the other staff
Tell the guests he is already the butler
Wait without saying anything until he is noticed
questions.why: Asking for the skills needed and taking training is the way to a promotion. Acting as if he already has the job or waiting silently does not help.

questions.q: Which qualification can Andre work for through HEART/NSTA Trust?
o: A pilot's licence
A tourism licence for his own villa
A degree in tourism economics
NVQ-J certificates in hospitality units
questions.why: HEART/NSTA Trust trains workers and awards NVQ-J certificates through accredited centres. A tourism licence is for a business, not a person.

questions.q: Which action best shows the manager that Andre is ready for more responsibility?
o: Telling other staff that he is better than the manager
Doing the butler's tasks without being asked or trained
Leaving his gardening to watch the guests all day
Doing his own job reliably and taking extra tasks when asked
questions.why: Reliability in the present job, plus willingness to learn extra tasks, is what managers look for before promotion. Taking over another job unasked causes problems.

questions.q: Which airport will the visitor probably use to fly home from Kingston?
o: Sangster International Airport
Norman Manley International Airport
Ken Jones Aerodrome in Port Antonio
Negril Aerodrome
questions.why: Norman Manley International Airport serves Kingston. Sangster is in Montego Bay.

questions.q: In which parish is Port Royal?
o: St Ann
Portland
Kingston and St Andrew
Westmoreland
questions.why: Port Royal is a historic town on the Kingston harbour, in the parish of Kingston and St Andrew.

questions.q: What does Shaniqua say about a MICE group?
o: Meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions
Music, islands, cruises and entertainment
Markets, inns, cafés and events
Money, insurance, cars and exports
questions.why: MICE stands for meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions: business-event tourism.

questions.q: A group of runners from Florida travels to Jamaica for a road race. Which type of tourism is this?
o: Sports tourism
Heritage tourism
Medical tourism
Cruise tourism
questions.why: Visitors who travel to take part in or watch a sport are sports tourists. Heritage tourism is about historic places, and cruise tourism is about visitors who arrive by ship.

questions.q: Which organisation markets and promotes Jamaica as a place to visit?
o: TPDCo
HEART/NSTA Trust
The local health department
The Jamaica Tourist Board
questions.why: The JTB markets Jamaica. TPDCo improves and checks the tourism product and trains workers, and HEART/NSTA Trust trains workers for jobs.

questions.q: A social media post says a new rule starts tomorrow. What should a villa worker do?
o: Tell guests at once, since the post is online
Check an official source and the manager first
Ignore it, as online posts are never true
Ask other guests whether they heard it too
questions.why: Social media is not always reliable. Check an official source and the manager so that guests get correct information.

questions.q: A cruise ship is in port at Falmouth for the day. What do its passengers most likely want from local tourism workers?
o: A fortnight's stay in a villa near the port
Help to arrange a month of travel around every parish
A short tour, craft shopping and a meal before the ship leaves
A place to leave the ship for good and settle on the island
questions.why: Cruise passengers spend a day or part of a day ashore, so they want short, well-timed activities. They are not stopover guests.
